quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle could push you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they can make oncoming vehicles appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do?

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle steady.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You can usually control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses underneath.

questions.explanation: Good eye or face shield protection must be free of scratches, resist breakage, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air flow to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help protect you from serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also provides protection. A sweatshirt does not offer adequate protection in a crash.

questions.question: When should you wear hearing protection?

options.text: It is not needed if you wear a helmet.

questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even when wearing a helmet. You should wear hearing protection on all rides.

questions.question: What can help reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your intentions, keep space around your bike, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have space to steer away.
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the transmission should be in:
questions.explanation: Put your transmission in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that comes on when the ignition is on and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear brightly-colored, reflective clothing anytime you ride, day or night.

questions.question: If another driver looks directly at you, what does that mean?

options.text: They may not have actually seen you.
They will always give you the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver has seen you just because they looked at you. A driver can look directly at a motorcycle and still not notice it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This white sign with red and black markings tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow-moving vehicles going slower than 25 mph, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, why does a motorcycle rider have an advantage over a car driver?

options.text: A motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
A motorcycle can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid opening doors and people.
Motorcycles can stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid opening doors and people.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, you can ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What kind of gloves should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of tough material. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It can be dangerous to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When you drink alcohol quickly, what happens?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen at intersections. The main cause is a car driver failing to give the motorcycle rider the right-of-way.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Riding in tire tracks left by cars gives you the best grip.

questions.question: How fast does the body remove alcohol?
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies remove about one drink per hour. This rate varies by person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: How should passengers hold on?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to grip your hips, waist, or belt firmly. Passengers can also use secure handholds if available.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in your direction.
